clue.text: People in support through love of magician

parts.note: supporters of a motion are the pros, as in pros and cons
per means by way of or through, as in per post
love is nil in tennis scoring, a round O

explanation.surface: A magician owes his success to the backing of supportive people.
explanation.walkthrough: PROSPERO is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Prospero is the exiled duke and sorcerer who conjures the storm in The Tempest.

clue.text: Snatch leather with soft coating

parts.note: kid is soft leather made from young goatskin, as in kid gloves
nap is the soft raised pile on cloth such as velvet

explanation.surface: Grab a piece of leather that has a soft surface finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to snatch and carry them off by force.

clue.text: Caught taking her water supply from river

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a well is a shaft sunk to draw water

explanation.surface: Someone is caught drawing water from a river for her household.
explanation.walkthrough: The CHERWELL is the river that flows through Oxford into the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherwell is an English river, a tributary of the Thames famous for punting at Oxford.

clue.text: See 10
Wall to speak directly to 10 5 down 21

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
to utter is to say out loud

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: a wall that addresses a theatre company directly.
explanation.walkthrough: 10, 5 down and 21 together make NORTHERN BROADSIDES, the Halifax theatre company that BARRIE RUTTER, the actor-director, founded and led.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrie Rutter founded the Yorkshire theatre company Northern Broadsides and was its artistic director for twenty-five years.

clue.text: Ladies of the Lakes?

definitions.meaning: the Norfolk ... are a network of shallow lakes and waterways in eastern England

explanation.surface: Women who belong to a lakeland district.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both women in US slang and the shallow lakes of Norfolk and Suffolk.

clue.text: Little fellow and little fool keeping time

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the fool's word encloses the time

parts.note: simp is a shortened simpleton, a fool
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A small man and a silly little friend manage to keep time together.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is a dismissive name for a small, slight person.

clue.text: Dad's part has promise

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a role is an actor's part in a play

explanation.surface: Father's role in the family carries a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole originally means a prisoner's word of honour, a solemn promise not to escape.

clue.text: Skimp on publicity for nude show with king to be model

indicators.note: show tells the solver to display these letters in a new arrangement

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R in royal signatures
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: A nude show where a king models is played down rather than promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' turns NUDE into UNDE, followed by REX and POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To underexpose something, figuratively, is to give it too little publicity or attention.

clue.text: Exploiting queen when unconscious, point to close relation

indicators.note: when unconscious places the exploiting of the queen inside a state of unconsciousness

parts.note: an unconscious patient is in a coma
to exploit something is to be using it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of an unconscious queen to point out a close relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' reads as 'while in a coma': USINGER goes inside COMA after its first two letters, then N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin german is a first cousin, the child of a parent's sibling, so a close relation.

clue.text: Air display (and not the Navy's) with pet food

parts.note: nor means and not
RN is the Royal Navy
lights are animal lungs, traditionally fed to cats and dogs

explanation.surface: A flying display without the Navy, laid on with pet food.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets are part of the wordplay, not an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern lights, the aurora borealis, are a glowing display in the night sky.

clue.text: Cutter also produces sound

indicators.note: sound tells the solver to say the phrase aloud and write what is heard

parts.note: adds means puts on in addition or also produces

explanation.surface: A cutting tool that also makes a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking tool with an arched blade set at right angles to its handle, used for cutting.

clue.text: Able to grasp things concerning birds in big building

indicators.note: in places the birds and concerning inside the big building

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building, such as a stately home
re means about or concerning
hens are female birds, farmyard fowl

explanation.surface: Birds in a large house have the ability to hold things.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehensile tail or limb is adapted for grasping and holding, like a monkey's tail.

clue.text: Work with mouse to contribute largely to 66 at bingo?

definitions.meaning: to press a computer mouse button twice rapidly
in bingo, 66 is called clickety-click, which is mostly two clicks

explanation.surface: A computer user's mouse habit makes up most of a bingo call.
explanation.walkthrough: Bingo callers have rhyming names for numbers; 66 is 'clickety-click', and two clicks give most of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-click is to press a mouse button twice in quick succession to open something.

clue.text: Special occasion, maybe third in recess

indicators.note: in puts the reworked word inside the recess

parts.note: a bay is a recess, as in a bay window

indicators.note: maybe suggests these letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A third special occasion might happen in an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special occasion' is the definition; 'maybe' is the anagram signal on 'third', and 'in' places the result within the recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is an annual special occasion celebrating the day someone was born.

clue.text: Rodent getting a large portion about lunchtime

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the portion goes round the time

parts.note: a chunk is a large piece or portion
1 pm is lunchtime, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A rodent getting a big helping around lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 in '1pm' is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipmunk is a small striped North American squirrel-like rodent.

clue.text: Sport of kings? I wonder

indicators.note: wonder as a verb means to wander mentally, here signalling the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Is this the sport of kings, I wonder?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport of kings' wants to be horse racing; 'wonder' rearranges KINGS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing is the sport of gliding down snow slopes on long runners.

clue.text: Half 11 plenty for enthusiast

indicators.note: half of the answer to 11 is kept, its first two letters dropped

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, a cutting tool
a lot means plenty

explanation.surface: Half past eleven is plenty for an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatical or extremely enthusiastic follower of a cause.

clue.text: Big building where ringers see and hear about bows put back right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the internet service goes round the bows

parts.note: Skype is the internet video calling service where callers see and hear each other

indicators.note: put back means the word for bows is written in reverse

parts.note: a bow is a curve, an arc

explanation.surface: A tall building where bell-ringers see and hear about bows being returned properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringers' means people making phone calls, not bell-ringers; 'put back' turns the bows and 'about' puts them inside, with the right's R at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyscraper is a very tall multi-storey building.

clue.text: Divers don't use towel?

definitions.meaning: divers here is the old adjective meaning various, several
to ... is to dry in the sun instead of with a towel

explanation.surface: Swimmers who skip the towel after their dive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or several, the same as the old adjective divers.

clue.text: See 5 across
Date in Rome for fishes

definitions.meaning: in the Roman calendar, the 15th of March, May, July and October, or the 13th of other months
an ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family, also called orfe

explanation.surface: A Roman date when fish are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The ides were a fixed day in the Roman calendar; ides is also the plural of a European fish.

clue.text: Sweet William, say, bringing incense to goddess shortly

indicators.note: to means attached to, so the incense comes after the goddess
shortly means cut short, so the goddess loses her final letter

parts.note: Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting
thus is frankincense, an aromatic resin

explanation.surface: A man named William brings incense to a goddess briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet William is a garden flower of the genus Dianthus, the pinks and carnations.

clue.text: Religious building goes ahead

definitions.meaning: a place of worship, as in Hindu or Jewish worship
at the side of the head, so it goes on ahead, read playfully

explanation.surface: A place of worship gets the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building for worship; the temples are also the flat sides of the head.

clue.text: See 9
Singularly little money for butter?

definitions.meaning: a trifling sum, and singularly asks for the one-word singular form
a nut ground to make a sandwich spread

explanation.surface: Very little money paid for butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is slang for a paltry sum, and the nut is ground into a popular spread.
